experiments/star-field/engine/frame/updates.ts

Per-frame scene updates driven by tickFrame — approach
Source src/experiments/star-field/engine/frame/updates.ts
UX surface Boot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

checkApproach

Proximity check — when the camera comes within a body's approach distance its dossier JSON prefetches via onApproach, once per body per session (the approached set). Selection prefetches too, so a slow drift-through and a direct nav click share one cache.

  • @param s Engine state.

updateLod

Detail level-of-detail — toggles each node's secondary geometry (shells, satellite pivots, the near-field star group) by camera distance so remote bodies draw as one primitive. Orbit radius counts toward size so a body's ring stays visible while the camera is still inside it. Galactic stars carry a farGlyph point glow that swaps with the near-field group — point glyph at chart distances, real photosphere on approach — the mirror of the solar collapse.

  • @param s Engine state.

updateStructures

Cosmic-hierarchy shell fade — hides the inside of every boundary bubble while the camera is deep within it. A huge fresnel shell viewed from the interior paints a bright silhouette over the whole sky (the giant cream-ball bug), so each structure's shell ramps to visible only once the camera has pulled back to 1.25–1.7× its radius.

  • @param s Engine state.

updateGalaxyClouds

Volumetric galaxy cloud fade — the Milky Way's particle disc is viewed from inside. Without distance attenuation the hundreds of thousands of additive points stack into an opaque glowing ball that swallows the view; fade them down while the camera is embedded, and ramp up as the camera pulls back far enough to read the disc as a whole. Only volumetric clouds carry the marker.

  • @param s Engine state.

updateStarCloud

Deep-field cloud camera fade — the real catalogue surrounds the Sun isotropically, so pulled far enough back it reads as a solid glowing sphere regardless of the per-star edge fade. While the camera is embedded the full density is correct (the local stellar neighborhood IS a volume); once outside, the cloud rolls down to a faint floor so it dissolves into the Milky Way disc instead of painting a ball.

  • @param s Engine state.

trackHover

Hover tracking — re-projects the hovered anchor each tick and reports canvas-space pixels so the DOM tooltip + leader line track orbiting bodies. The navigator-hover hint takes precedence over the raycast hover (the pointer is on the drawer) and resolves its stored anchor or shard record into a live world point, then an edge-clamped screen point that locates the body at any zoom level. Fires nothing when hover is idle (no per-frame DOM churn).

  • @param s Engine state.

updateDayNight

Day/night uniform feed — for every body whose shading depends on the sun direction (night-lights emissive gating, atmosphere rim shells) writes dir = normalize(sunPos − bodyPos) into the shared vector the material's TSL uniform wraps. anchorWorldPos's shared scratch is copied before the loop so the sun position survives each resolution.

  • @param s Engine state.

smoothstep

Local smoothstep helper — mirrors GLSL, no dependency on three.js.
